description: Team Beyond Earth 2026. I am a solo participant working on the NASA Space Apps Challenge. My chosen challenge is "A Guide to Interplanetary Survival: Map of Mars". I am focusing on creating a visual map to help understand survival on Mars. I am passionate about space exploration and web development. I am ready to work hard and create a great project!
summary:
Jezero Field Atlas is an interactive web atlas that I developed to help users explore Jezero Crater on Mars. I created a website with five thematic map layers: geological features, elevation and the ancient lakeshore, historical landing hazards, Perseverance rover exploration, and steep slopes. Users can switch between layers and click on marked points to discover important locations, their scientific significance, and NASA mission history.
My project addresses the challenge by bringing different types of Martian surface information together in one accessible interface. It helps users understand the landscape, explore geological features, and learn about terrain conditions that should be considered when planning future missions.
I believe this project is important because understanding the Martian surface is essential for safer and more effective exploration. By making NASA-based scientific information easier to access and understand, Jezero Field Atlas supports scientific learning and encourages better planning for future robotic and human missions to Mars.
details:
Jezero Field Atlas — Project Details

I independently developed Jezero Field Atlas, an interactive web-based guide to Jezero Crater on Mars. The project brings together scientific images and information from NASA missions in one accessible interface.

The website features five thematic map views: geological features, elevation and the ancient lakeshore, historical landing hazards, Perseverance rover exploration, and steep slopes. Users can switch between these views and select marked points to discover information about important locations, their history, and scientific significance.

I used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the website and create its interactive features. The project uses publicly available NASA imagery and scientific publications as its main references. It is designed to be simple to navigate, visually clear, and accessible through a web browser.

The main benefit is that users can explore different aspects of the Martian landscape without searching through multiple separate sources. The project supports science education and helps users understand terrain features that may be relevant to planning future exploration missions.

I considered scientific accuracy, ease of use, clear descriptions, and the importance of distinguishing historical spacecraft landing hazards from actual human surface safety. The map markers are illustrative and are not intended for precise navigation.
